experiences.name: Tacos al Pastor Crawl in La Condesa

experiences.location: Teotihuacán, State of Mexico (approx. 50 km northeast of Mexico City)

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to hotel in Centro Histórico via Metro Line 5 to Pantitlán, then transfer to Line 1 toward Observatorio, exit at Pino Suárez or Zócalo station (~45–60 min, ~$0.50 USD). Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely walk to the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral exterior (free entry) and the National Palace facade. Stroll through the surrounding streets of Centro Histórico to get your bearings and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the pedestrian street Calle Madero, lined with historic buildings and street performers. Visit the rooftop terrace of the Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for a free peek at the stunning Art Nouveau interior. Wind down with a relaxed dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan area — try a torta or tacos from street vendors near the Zócalo (~$2–4 USD)
meals.dinner: El Huequito on Calle Bolívar — famous for tacos al pastor, a local institution. Full meal under $6 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Use the afternoon to orient yourself. The Metro is the cheapest and fastest way to get around (~$0.25–0.50 USD per ride). Get a rechargeable Metro card at any station.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site (entry ~$4 USD), the ancient Aztec temple unearthed in the heart of Centro Histórico. The on-site museum is included in the ticket and is world-class. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the ruins and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio de Bellas Artes (free to enter the ground floor and admire the stunning Art Deco exterior; murals on upper floors ~$1.50 USD). Afterward, walk to the Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela (~15 min walk or short Metro ride) to browse handmade crafts — great for window shopping and understanding local culture without pressure to buy.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and explore the lit-up Zócalo at night — it's magical. Walk along Calle Regina, a pedestrian street with a lively local atmosphere, street food stalls, and affordable bars.

meals.breakfast: Café de Tacuba near the hotel — a historic Mexico City café open since 1912. Try chilaquiles or tamales with café de olla (~$5–7 USD)
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan — grab fresh juices, quesadillas, or a full comida corrida (set lunch menu with soup, main, and drink for ~$4–6 USD) at one of the market fondas
meals.dinner: Street tacos on Calle Regina or nearby — carnitas, barbacoa, or al pastor tacos at ~$0.50–1 USD each. Budget $3–5 USD for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays — if Day 2 falls on a Monday, swap with Day 3 activities. Most national museums in Mexico are free on Sundays for Mexican residents; as a tourist, entry fees are very low regardless.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán (Line 3 to Viveros or Coyoacán station, ~30 min, $0.50 USD). Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum 'La Casa Azul' — book tickets online in advance (~$12 USD, one of the pricier but most iconic cultural experiences in the city). Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Coyoacán's charming cobblestone streets, colorful colonial architecture, and local markets. Visit the Mercado de Coyoacán for a traditional lunch. Browse the artisan stalls in the central plaza (Jardín Centenario) and relax in the park — a favorite spot for locals on weekends.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via Metro. Visit the Eje Central area for a street food crawl — try memelas, tlayudas, or elotes (grilled corn). If interested, check out a free or low-cost cultural event; UNAM and local cultural centers often host free performances.

meals.breakfast: Grab tamales and atole from a street cart near the hotel before heading out (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Mercado de Coyoacán — tostadas de tinga or enchiladas at a market stall (~$3–5 USD). Try the famous tostadas at Tostadas Coyoacán stand.
meals.dinner: Comida corrida at a neighborhood fonda back in Centro Histórico (~$4–6 USD) or street food crawl (~$4–5 USD total)

day_by_day.notes: Coyoacán is a half-day to full-day neighborhood — it's very walkable and charming. Wear comfortable shoes. The Frida Kahlo Museum sells out fast; book at least a few days ahead online at museofridakahlo.org.mx.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Chapultepec (Line 1, Chapultepec station). Spend the morning in Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the world — entry to the park is free. Visit the Castillo de Chapultepec (National History Museum, ~$3.50 USD) for panoramic city views and fascinating Mexican history exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Museo Nacional de Antropología (one of the best anthropology museums in the world, ~$4.50 USD). Spend 2–3 hours marveling at Aztec, Maya, and other pre-Columbian artifacts including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. This is a must-see cultural highlight of Mexico City.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Condesa or Roma neighborhood (short Metro or walk from Chapultepec) — these trendy, tree-lined barrios are great for an evening stroll. Window-shop, people-watch, and enjoy the local vibe before heading back to Centro Histórico.

meals.breakfast: Tortas at a local shop near the hotel (~$2–3 USD) or yogurt and fruit from a street vendor
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a nearby market to eat in Chapultepec Park, or grab tacos from vendors inside the park (~$3–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Mercado Medellín in Roma (short Metro ride) — a vibrant local market with incredible food stalls. Try Caribbean-Mexican fusion dishes or classic Mexican plates (~$4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Chapultepec Park is enormous — wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water. The Anthropology Museum alone can take 3–4 hours if explored thoroughly; prioritize the Mexica (Aztec) and Maya halls if time is limited. Both museums are free on Sundays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de la Merced or Mercado Jamaica (take Metro Line 1 to Merced station) — massive traditional markets where locals shop for produce, spices, flowers, and food. This is one of the most authentic local experiences in the city. Grab a hearty breakfast at one of the market fondas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Centro Histórico for any last-minute sightseeing. Visit the Secretaría de Educación Pública (SEP) building on República de Argentina street — free entry to see Diego Rivera's stunning murals covering the interior courtyard walls, a hidden gem that most tourists miss. Afterward, browse the bookstores and shops along Donceles Street (known as the 'Street of Books').
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Centro Histórico. Pick up any last souvenirs from street vendors around the Zócalo (haggling is acceptable). Spend your last evening enjoying the lit-up historic center, grab a mezcal or pulque at a local cantina, and reflect on the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full market breakfast at Mercado de la Merced — huevos rancheros, beans, tortillas, and fresh juice (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Pozole or menudo at a traditional restaurant in Centro Histórico (~$4–6 USD) — hearty, traditional, and perfect for a last lunch
meals.dinner: Cantina La Peninsular or similar traditional cantina near the Zócalo — order a classic dish like mole enchiladas or chiles en nogada (seasonal) with a local beer or mezcal (~$7–10 USD for a special farewell meal)

day_by_day.notes: If departing the next morning, pack your bags tonight and confirm transport to the airport. The Metro to the airport (Line 5, Terminal Aérea station) takes about 45–60 min and costs ~$0.50 USD — the most budget-friendly option. Keep some pesos for any last-minute expenses. Average daily budget for this trip: ~$25–40 USD per day including food, transport, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Check in to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico and freshen up after the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely orientation walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace exterior. Pop into the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's iconic murals depicting Mexican history — free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Calle Regina and Madero pedestrian street as the neighborhood comes alive at dusk. Explore the lit-up historic facades and browse artisan street stalls.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or at airport on arrival day.
meals.lunch: Café de Tacuba (historic restaurant near the Zócalo) — a Mexico City institution since 1912. Try the enchiladas and a classic agua fresca. Mid-range, ~$12–18 USD per person.
meals.dinner: El Cardenal (Palacio de Iturbide branch) — celebrated for traditional Mexican cuisine. Order the caldo tlalpeño and tamales. ~$18–25 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light since you arrive at 13:00. Allow 45–60 minutes for the taxi or metro ride from the airport to Centro Histórico. Comfortable walking shoes are essential from day one.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Templo Mayor, the excavated Aztec temple complex right in the heart of Centro Histórico. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the ruins and the excellent on-site museum showcasing pre-Hispanic artifacts. Entry ~$5 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Mercado de San Juan (20-minute walk or short metro ride) — a beloved gourmet market full of local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh juices, and international ingredients. Browse and snack. Afterward, visit the Museo Franz Mayer, a stunning 16th-century building housing decorative arts and applied crafts. Entry ~$4 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the trendy Barrio Lagunilla and its antique market area, then wind down in the quieter streets of Centro with a mezcal tasting at a local cantina.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café — try Panadería Rosetta on Calle Havre for pastries and coffee (~$6–9 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Mercado de San Juan food stalls — try tlayudas, fresh ceviche, or a torta. Budget-friendly at ~$6–10 USD.
meals.dinner: Hostería de Santo Domingo (oldest restaurant in Mexico City) — try the chiles en nogada if in season, or the classic mole. ~$15–22 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays — if Day 2 falls on a Monday, swap with the Museo Franz Mayer visit or explore the Alameda Central park instead.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Coyoacán (about 40 minutes from Centro) — a charming bohemian neighborhood. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul), the iconic blue house where Frida Kahlo was born and lived. Book tickets online in advance. Entry ~$13 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Coyoacán's colorful streets and central plaza (Jardín Centenario). Browse the Mercado de Artesanías de Coyoacán for handmade crafts, textiles, and souvenirs. Visit the nearby Museo León Trotsky for a fascinating historical detour (~$4 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and enjoy a rooftop drink at one of the boutique hotel bars overlooking the Zócalo — the illuminated cathedral at night is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Café El Jarocho in Coyoacán — a legendary coffee spot beloved by locals. Grab a café de olla and a pastry. ~$4–6 USD.
meals.lunch: Los Danzantes in Coyoacán — excellent modern Mexican cuisine with great mezcal selection. Try the duck in mole negro. ~$18–25 USD per person.
meals.dinner: La Casa de las Sirenas (rooftop terrace near the Zócalo) — traditional Mexican dishes with stunning cathedral views. ~$20–28 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online before your trip. Coyoacán is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take an Uber or organized tour (about 50 minutes) to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Aztec city of pyramids. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon and walk the Avenue of the Dead. Arrive early to beat crowds. Entry ~$6 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city by early afternoon. Stop in the neighborhood of Tepito or La Merced market area for an authentic local market experience — one of the largest traditional markets in Latin America, full of spices, produce, and street food.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the historic Alameda Central park at golden hour, then visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau exterior and check if any evening performances or exhibitions are scheduled. Entry to the building is free; events vary in price.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before departure — or grab tamales and atole from a street vendor near the hotel (~$3–5 USD).
meals.lunch: At Teotihuacán, dine at La Gruta restaurant — a dramatic cave restaurant near the pyramids serving traditional Mexican dishes. ~$15–22 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico (inside a beautiful courtyard in Centro) — upscale-casual Mexican regional cuisine. Try the cochinita pibil or the black bean soup. ~$18–26 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Start the Teotihuacán trip by 8:00–9:00 AM to avoid midday heat and crowds. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water — the site is very exposed. The pyramids involve significant climbing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec Park (about 20 minutes from Centro by metro or Uber) — arguably the best anthropology museum in Latin America. Allow 2–3 hours for highlights including the Aztec Sun Stone and Mayan artifacts. Entry ~$5 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the beautiful Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) — a massive urban park perfect for a relaxed walk. Visit the Castillo de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Castle) perched on a hill with panoramic city views and fascinating history as a former imperial palace. Entry ~$4 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a final evening. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at artisan shops near the Zócalo, then enjoy a farewell dinner at a spot that best captures the essence of Mexican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café de la Parroquia or a local taquería near the hotel — try chilaquiles or huevos rancheros. ~$7–11 USD.
meals.lunch: Tacos at El Hidalguense near Chapultepec — famous for barbacoa tacos served only until they run out. A true local experience. ~$8–12 USD.
meals.dinner: Contramar (if budget allows a slight splurge) or return to a favorite spot from the week. Contramar is celebrated for its tuna tostadas and grilled fish. ~$25–35 USD per person — a memorable farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is closed on Mondays. Chapultepec Park is very popular on weekends — expect more crowds on Saturdays and Sundays. This is a great day to reflect on the trip and do any final souvenir shopping.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico via private luxury transfer. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely orientation walk through the historic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Visit the stunning Catedral Metropolitana and admire the exterior of the Palacio Nacional. Stop at the Templo Mayor archaeological site for a guided private tour of the ancient Aztec ruins and its world-class on-site museum.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset rooftop drinks at a terrace bar overlooking the Zócalo — try the Gran Hotel Ciudad de México's rooftop for panoramic views. Dinner at Contramar or a reservation at Azul Histórico, a refined Mexican cuisine restaurant set in a beautiful colonial courtyard in Centro Histórico.

meals.lunch: Light welcome snack or room service at the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico — elegant Mexican cuisine in a colonial garden setting; try the mole negro and regional mezcal selection

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Book Templo Mayor guided tour ahead of time for a private experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Palacio Nacional, including Diego Rivera's sweeping murals depicting Mexican history. Follow with a visit to the Museo del Templo Mayor for a deeper dive into Aztec civilization. Walk through the charming streets of Centro Histórico, exploring the Mercado de Artesanías and the ornate Palacio de Bellas Artes exterior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio de Bellas Artes for a curated interior tour of its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and world-class murals by Orozco, Siqueiros, and Rivera. Afterward, stroll through Alameda Central park. Visit the Museo Franz Mayer, a premier decorative arts museum housed in a 16th-century hospital, showcasing colonial Mexican crafts and design.
day_by_day.evening: Pre-dinner cocktails at Bar La Opera, a legendary Belle Époque cantina in Centro Histórico with a bullet hole in the ceiling allegedly made by Pancho Villa. Dinner at Pujol (reserve well in advance) — one of Latin America's finest restaurants, offering an iconic tasting menu celebrating modern Mexican cuisine and ancient ingredients.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a full traditional Mexican breakfast with chilaquiles, fresh fruit, and café de olla
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Cardenal, a beloved institution in Centro Histórico serving refined traditional Mexican dishes since 1969
meals.dinner: Pujol — world-renowned tasting menu featuring the iconic Mole Madre; pair with a curated Mexican wine or mezcal flight

day_by_day.notes: Pujol reservations must be made weeks in advance. Palacio Nacional is free but private guide enhances the experience significantly. Dress code at Pujol is smart casual.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Coyoacán neighborhood. Begin with a visit to the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) — book a premium timed-entry ticket or private after-hours tour for an intimate experience. Explore the cobblestone streets, colorful colonial architecture, and lively Jardín Centenario.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museo Anahuacalli, Diego Rivera's dramatic volcanic stone museum housing his vast pre-Columbian artifact collection — a lesser-known gem. Continue to the nearby San Ángel neighborhood for a walk through its elegant 17th-century streets, the Jardín de la Bombilla, and the Bazar del Sábado artisan market area (open Saturdays). Stop at the Museo Casa Estudio Diego Rivera y Frida Kahlo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico by private car. Evening at leisure — explore the illuminated historic center on a private night walking tour. Dinner at Quintonil, another pinnacle of contemporary Mexican fine dining, celebrated for its use of indigenous vegetables and herbs.

meals.breakfast: Café El Jarocho in Coyoacán — a legendary neighborhood coffee institution; pair with pan dulce from a nearby bakery
meals.lunch: El Tizoncito in Coyoacán — credited as birthplace of the taco al pastor; enjoy an authentic, casual yet iconic lunch
meals.dinner: Quintonil — innovative tasting menu with a focus on seasonal and foraged Mexican ingredients; exceptional natural wine list

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum requires advance booking — private or after-hours tours available through luxury concierge services. Coyoacán is about 30–40 minutes from Centro Histórico by private car.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Teotihuacán — depart early by private luxury vehicle with a certified archaeologist guide. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead. Enjoy exclusive access or a sunrise private tour if arranged through concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán's lesser-visited Palace of Quetzalpapálotl and the vibrant murals of Tetitla. On the return journey, stop at a traditional pulque hacienda or a local mezcal producer for a private tasting and education session on Mexico's ancient fermented beverages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico. Relax at the hotel with a spa treatment if available. Dinner at Dulce Patria (in Polanco, a short drive away) — Chef Martha Ortiz's theatrical and artistic interpretation of Mexican gastronomy in a lush, visually stunning setting.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — light and energizing; request a traditional Mexican spread with tamales and atole
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel or a local caterer, enjoyed at Teotihuacán with views of the pyramids — arrange through concierge
meals.dinner: Dulce Patria — signature dishes include cochinita pibil and chiles en nogada (seasonal); vibrant cocktail program with Mexican spirits

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 7:00–7:30 AM to beat crowds at Teotihuacán. Private guide and transport are essential for a premium experience. Comfortable walking shoes and sun protection are a must.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Mexico City — visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec, arguably the finest anthropology museum in the world. Arrange a private guided tour to explore the Aztec Sun Stone, Mayan galleries, and Olmec colossal heads without the crowds. Stroll through the Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the Americas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Polanco neighborhood — browse luxury boutiques, galleries, and the Presidente Masaryk boulevard. Visit the Museo Jumex, a world-class contemporary art museum with an impressive Latin American collection. Stop for coffee and pastries at one of Polanco's elegant cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Rosetta, Chef Elena Reygadas' celebrated restaurant in a stunning 19th-century mansion in Colonia Roma — a perfect blend of Italian inspiration and Mexican ingredients. After dinner, enjoy a final mezcal nightcap at Expendio de Pulques Finos or a craft cocktail at a rooftop bar in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — indulge in a full traditional spread: huevos rancheros, fresh tropical fruits, pan dulce, and café de olla
meals.lunch: Lardo in Colonia Roma — Chef Elena Reygadas' casual sister restaurant; outstanding wood-fired dishes and natural wines
meals.dinner: Rosetta — tasting menu or à la carte; signature dishes include hoja santa pasta and seasonal Mexican-Italian fusion; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Museo Nacional de Antropología requires at least 2–3 hours; private guide highly recommended. Pack and arrange late checkout or luggage storage with the hotel if departing in the evening. Confirm departure transfer the night before.
